name: The Invisible Man
description: A scientist who discovers the secret of invisibility

film.title: The Invisible Man
film.note: Visual effects by John P. Fulton, who used black velvet and optical mattes to make Rains disappear.

legend: Invisibility is an ancient fantasy. In Plato's Republic, the shepherd Gyges finds a ring that makes him unseen and uses it to seduce a queen and seize a throne, and Plato asks whether anyone would stay honest if no one could watch. Wells gave that question a scientific costume: his student Griffin changes his body's refractive index until light passes straight through him, then discovers that being unseen is lonely, cold and maddening.

myths.claim: Griffin can become visible again whenever he likes.
myths.explanation: He never finds a cure. His body only becomes visible again as he dies.

myths.claim: Food he eats stays visible until it's digested.
myths.explanation: In the novel Griffin explains he must hide after meals, because undigested food shows inside him.

myths.claim: Claude Rains's face is seen through most of the 1933 film.
myths.explanation: His face appears only in the last moments. For the rest he is bandages, goggles and that famous voice.

myths.claim: In the film, a drug called monocane drives Griffin mad.
myths.explanation: The screenplay added monocane as the cause of his madness. Wells's Griffin was already bitter and cruel.

quotes.text: The stranger came early in February, one wintry day, through a biting wind and a driving snow.
quotes.speaker: Narrator

quotes.text: An invisible man is a man of power.
quotes.speaker: Griffin

powers: Free run of any locked room
legacy: The Invisible Man Returns (1940), with Vincent Price
Abbott and Costello Meet the Invisible Man (1951)
facts: Griffin must go naked to be fully invisible, even in an English winter
Snow, rain, fog and smoke reveal his outline
Food he eats stays visible until it is digested
Claude Rains's face appears only in the final moments of the 1933 film
John P. Fulton used black velvet and mattes to make Rains vanish on screen
Wells's Griffin has no first name; the film called him Jack
Plato told of an invisibility ring, the Ring of Gyges, over 2,000 years earlier
hostIntro: Tonight's guest insisted on coming to the studio, and I think he's here. Somewhere. If you feel a draught, that's probably him.
